description.narrative: Support building, protecting, and utilizing human capital in Bhutan

The development objective of Human Capital Recovery and Resilience Program for Results Project is to Support building, protecting, and utilizing human capital in Bhutan. The Program supports a subset of the Government's 12th Five-Year Plan (12th FYP) by strengthening the implementation of selected priority activities aligned primarily with National Key Result Areas (NKRAs) 7 and 11, which focus on improving access to and quality of education and enhancing employment outcomes. The Program also incorporates interventions introduced to mitigate the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. Under this framework, the Program aims to (i) ensure a strong foundation for a lifecycle approach to boosting future human capital accumulation, (ii) support economic and human capital recovery in the post-COVID-19 context, and (iii) increase human capital resilience to future shocks. The Program is organized around four Results Areas. Results Area 1: Expanded Access and Professionalization of Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) supports equitable access to quality ECCD through the development of a national ECCD plan, expansion of services for urban poor and rural populations, capacity building of ECCD facilitators, and strengthening of quality assurance systems. Results Area 2: Digitization of Education for Improved Student Outcomes focuses on strengthening equity, inclusiveness, and resilience in education by supporting curriculum digitization in core subjects, enhancing digital pedagogy competencies of teachers, expanding remote learning facilities, reducing the digital divide, and promoting climate awareness in schools. Results Area 3: Improved Employment and Inclusion Outcomes aims to enhance inclusion and gainful employment by increasing participation of women and rural job seekers in Ministry of Labour and Human Resources (MoLHR) programs, strengthening the employment orientation of skills training, and supporting entrepreneurship through incubation, training, and improved access to finance. Results Area 4: Enhanced Resilience of Jobseekers seeks to strengthen systems for timely recovery support during environmental and economic shocks by improving service delivery and coordination through a single-intake window, enhancing interoperability across programs and institutions, supporting labor market readiness, and integrating climate resilience strategies into MoLHR program design and delivery. Collectively, these Results Areas contribute to sustained improvements in education, employment, and human capital resilience in line with the objectives of the 12th FYP.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.1, Schedule 2 of the FA: The Recipient shall vest the responsibility for the Program in MoESD and MoICE, respectively.To this end, MoESD and MoICEshall, within two (2) months of the Effective Date, designate a focal officer within each of MoESD andMoICE respectively, to serve as the focal unit in carrying out the day-to-day implementation of the Program activities carriedunder their respective authority throughout the period of implementation of the Program, including compiling data on results andevidence on achievement of DLRs for submission to the Independent Verification Agent and the Bank.

Section I.A.2, Schedule 2 of the FA: The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, (or such otherdate which the Association has confirmed in writing to the Recipient is reasonable and acceptable under the circumstances), adoptthe Implementation Guidance Note in form and substance acceptable to the Association, and implement the Program in accordance withthe provisions of the Implementation Guidance Note.

Section I.B.2, Schedule 2 of the FA: The Recipient shall recruit no later than two (2) weeks after the Effective Date, (or suchother date which the Association has confirmed in writing to the Recipient is reasonable and acceptable under the circumstances)one or more independent verification agents on the basis of terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to theAssociation (“Independent Verification Agent”), as needed to verify the evidence supporting the achievement of all DLRs and certifythe fulfillment of such DLRs as set forth in Schedule 4 to the Financing Agreement.

Section V, Schedule 2 of the FA: The Recipient, through the MoESD, shall ensure that the collection, use, and processing (includingtransfers to third parties) of any Personal Data collected under this Project shall be done in accordance with the data protectionprinciples contained in the Information, Communication, and Media Act of Bhutan 2018 and applicable best international practice,ensuring legitimate, appropriate, and proportionate treatment of such data.
